newsitem.title: USA: Sixty percent of U.S. sex offenders freed on parole.
newsitem.headline: Sixty percent of U.S. sex offenders freed on parole.

text.p: Nearly 60 percent of the 234,000 convicted sex offenders under the jurisdiction of U.S. corrections officials had been released on parole or probation in 1994, the Justice Department reported on Sunday.

The report by the agency's information-gathering Bureau of Justice Statistics said an estimated 134,300 offenders had been released into the community on conditional supervision, such as parole or probation.
The remaining 99,300 offenders convicted of rape or sexual assault remained in local jails or state or federal prisons.
Sex offenders comprise nearly 10 percent of the state prison population, more than three percent in local jails and one percent in federal prisons, according to the report.
In a statement issued by the White House, President Clinton said the report served as "a warning that we must continue working to ensure that our children are safe from sex offenders."

Clinton, who signed community notification and state registry laws for sex offenders, vowed in the next year to add to the efforts "to reduce sexual violence and provide greater safety to children and security to parents."
The report gave the first national estimate of the size of the convicted, sex-offender population under the jurisdiction of correctional authorities.
Among the report's other findings, which are consistent with earlier conclusions, are the following:
-- The number of rapes and sexual assaults reported by victims in 1995 fell sharply from the level two years earlier.
-- Only 33 percent of the rape and sexual assault victims in 1994 and 1995 said they reported the crime to the police.

-- Most imprisoned sex offenders knew their victims. For rape, about 30 percent of the offenders said their victims had been strangers while 15 percent of the sexual assault offenders said they had no prior relationship with their victims.
-- Almost 60 percent of the incidents took place in the victim's home or the home of a friend, relative or neighbour.
